refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: A scheduler unit runs a provider that attaches a BPF CPU scheduler to a cgroup v2 subtree. The instance name identifies the target slice without its .slice suffix. For example, batch@build.scheduler targets build.slice. The slice selects this instance using Scheduler= as described in systemd.slice5.

Starting a service in the subtree pulls in the target slice and its selected schedulers. The system manager starts each parent before its children and waits for confirmation of the attachments before starting service commands. The root slice selects the host scheduler. Each parent provider must support child attachments to run schedulers further down the tree. Stopping a scheduler detaches its active descendants. Services already running continue under the closest surviving ancestor scheduler. Detaching the root restores the kernel's default scheduling policy.

refsect1.title: Options
refsect1.para: The [Scheduler] section accepts the following settings:

listitem.para: The provider command to run. Exactly one command is required. The provider must implement the Scheduler Provider Protocol. An absolute executable path adds mount dependencies for that path.
Time to wait for the provider to attach and confirm readiness. Defaults to DefaultTimeoutStartSec= from systemd-system.conf5.

refsect1.title: Examples

example.title: Run a separate scheduler for build services
example.para: Starting compile.service activates partition@-.scheduler followed by partition@build.scheduler. Inspect the latter with systemctl status partition@build.scheduler.

refsect1.para: For a host root scheduler, make the provider and its dependencies available at switch-root. Use RequiresMountsFor= for additional paths as necessary. A service that needs the scheduler cannot make that scheduler's loader available. With a systemd-based initrd supporting rd.systemd.break=pre-switch-root, use its console to restore the executable under /sysroot or clear Scheduler= in the affected host slices before continuing boot.
